stem: A 33-year-old woman presents with complaints of progressive loss of vision in the right halves of both eyes. Where is the lesion located in the optic pathway?
explanation: Loss of vision in the right halves of both visual fields (right homonymous hemianopia) is caused by a lesion of the left optic tract (or left radiation or occipital cortex). A chiasmal lesion gives bitemporal hemianopia.

stem: A 2-month-old infant was brought by this mother's complaints of inability to open the eyes in light and excessive watering. The clinical picture is given below. What is the most probable diagnosis?
explanation: A baby with watering, photophobia (inability to open eyes in light) and a large hazy cornea has congenital glaucoma (buphthalmos). Treatment is surgical, with goniotomy or trabeculotomy.

stem: A patient presents with abdominal pain and distension. An X-ray was taken which showed dilated bowel loops as given in the image below. Identify the segment involved?
explanation: Dilated bowel loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the whole lumen (a feathery, stacked-coin look) are jejunal loops. The ileum has a smooth outline, and the colon haustra don't cross completely.

stem: An alcoholic patient presented with itchy lesions as shown in the image. He also has a red-colored beefy tongue. Which of the following histories would you like to ask/elicit in this patient additionally?
options: Ask for diarrhea and a history of memory loss
Ask for diarrhea, thiamine deficiency features, and detailed dietary history
explanation: A beefy red tongue, a photosensitive itchy rash (Casal necklace) in an alcoholic suggests pellagra (niacin deficiency), characterised by diarrhoea, dermatitis and dementia. Ask for diarrhoea and memory loss.

stem: A 15-year-old girl is not compliant with spectacles for her myopic astigmatism. What would be the appropriate management in her case?
explanation: A non-compliant 15-year-old with myopic astigmatism should be given spherical equivalent spectacles or contact lenses. Refractive surgery (LASIK) is deferred until 18 years when the refraction is stable.

stem: A child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia undergoes prophylactic irradiation prior autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Which of the following will be the least affected?
explanation: Rapidly dividing cells (bone marrow precursors, intestinal epithelium, spermatogonia) are most radiosensitive according to the law of Bergonie and Tribondeau. Neurons are post-mitotic cells and are the least affected.

stem: The enzymes that convert pyruvate to acetyl CoA are given in the diagram. What are the enzymes marked as E1 and E2 respectively?
explanation: In the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex E1 is pyruvate dehydrogenase (using thiamine pyrophosphate), E2 is dihydrolipoyl transacetylase (lipoic acid, CoA), and E3 is dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase (FAD, NAD).

stem: A 5 year old boy presented with easy fatigability, irritability and inability to concentrate. Labs revealed the following findings a and b (light and oil immersion respectively) on the bone marrow aspiration. Which of the following is the most likely enzyme deficient in this condition?
explanation: A child with fatigue, and a bone marrow smear showing macrophages with crumpled tissue paper cytoplasm (Gaucher cells) has Gaucher disease, caused by deficiency of glucocerebrosidase.

stem: What is the most common complication associated with the following abnormality?
explanation: The condition shown is a proptosis or lagophthalmos with an eye that does not close fully, so the commonest complication is exposure keratopathy, as the cornea dries and ulcerates.

stem: During the clinical examination of the nervous system, which of the following nerves can be tested by touching the highlighted structure?
explanation: Touching the posterior third of the tongue or the pharyngeal wall tests the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX), the afferent limb of the gag reflex, with the vagus (X) as the efferent limb.

stem: A 7-year-old presented with a white pupillary reflex for which enucleation was done. The histopathological examination of the specimen showed Flexner Winterstein rosettes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (true rosettes with a central lumen) are the histological hallmark of retinoblastoma, which presents with leukocoria (white pupillary reflex) in children under 5 years.

stem: An industrial worker was admitted to the hospital after an eye injury sustained while cutting stone with a hammer and iron chisel. A foreign body was suspected to be impacted in his eye. Which investigation can be detrimental to this patient?
explanation: For a suspected metallic intraocular foreign body (iron chisel fragment), MRI is contraindicated because a magnetic foreign body may move. CT is the investigation of choice. The key marks MRI as the answer, so verify the question wording.

stem: A 34-year-old female patient presented to the outpatient department with migratory arthritis and examination revealed a pan-systolic murmur. An echocardiography was performed which was suggestive of mitral regurgitation. A biopsy specimen was obtained and the image is provided below. What is the most likely lesion shown in the histopathology slide?
explanation: Migratory arthritis and mitral regurgitation is acute rheumatic fever with carditis. The pathological hallmark is the Aschoff body, a granuloma with Anitschkow (caterpillar) cells and giant cells.

stem: A pap smear taken from a patient revealed hyperchromatic nuclei, irregular nuclear borders, and low maturation index involving the whole thickness but did not breach the basement membrane. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Hyperchromatic nuclei with irregular borders involving the whole thickness of the epithelium but not breaching the basement membrane is carcinoma in situ (high-grade dysplasia, CIN 3). The key marks dysplasia.

stem: A 70-year-old female patient presents with pain in the thigh during walking. Investigation reveals the following finding as given below. What will be the best surgical management? PTA: Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty
explanation: Thigh claudication in an elderly woman with long-segment aortoiliac or femoral disease on angiography is treated surgically with aortofemoral bypass for extensive aorto-iliac occlusive disease. Short stenoses suit angioplasty.

stem: According to the CEAP classification, What will be the C stage in this patient?
explanation: CEAP clinical class C2 is varicose veins of 3 mm or more, and the suffix A denotes asymptomatic. Hence C2A for asymptomatic varicose veins.

stem: 18. A 25-year-old patient presents with abdominal pain and fever for 3 days duration. The chest X-ray in the erect position is given below. What will be the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Fever and abdominal pain with free air under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray (pneumoperitoneum) is a hollow viscus perforation.

stem: In a patient with abdominal pain and sterile pyuria, what is the finding shown in the image given?
explanation: Sterile pyuria with abdominal pain and a small calcified, non-functioning kidney on imaging is putty kidney (autonephrectomy) of renal tuberculosis. Staghorn calculi are branching stones.
